subject: PocketTier swap — optional add-ons and downgrade path
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@medsentry.com>
Date: 2026-08-15 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PocketTier proposal and optional add-ons (follow-up)

Hi Alyssa,

Great to speak yesterday — thanks again for walking me through the main burst patterns for your triage worker pipeline. As promised, I attached a tailored PocketTier proposal (PDF) and a simple addon matrix that shows how feature packs map to throughput and latency SLOs.

Quick summary:
- Core PocketTier: baseline throughput for async inference, prefix caching, and standard routing.
- Add-on: RealTime Burst (3x short-term throughput for high-priority jobs) — priced as an optional monthly bolt-on.
- Add-on: Private-Log Retention (90d) — required for audit-aligned pipelines.

Two items you flagged I wanted to confirm here: downgrade path and discount structure.
1) Downgrade path: you can move from PocketTier -> Slimline within a single billing cycle with prorated credits for unused reserved capacity; we keep feature flags intact but certain add-ons like RealTime Burst are not available on Slimline. There is a 2-week cooldown after downgrades before capacity reallocation completes.
2) Discounting: we typically offer volume-based tier discounts on annual commits. For new pilots we can provide an introductory 10% commit credit for the first 3 months if you sign a 12-month agreement. Deeper multi-year discounts need commercial review.

I've attached the files; let me know if you want me to loop in Kimberly for commercial terms or Ben for any capacity planning questions.

Next step: If this looks good, I can push a formal quote and DocuSign for signature.

Best,
Sergio

Thanks Sergio — appreciate the clear summary and the materials. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we circulate to procurement: 

- Downgrade cooldown: two weeks is fine, can you confirm whether any data (logs/KV cache) is kept accessible during the cooldown window? We need to retain quick access for on-call debugging.
- RealTime Burst pricing: can you share an example calculation for a 50K-token/day burst usage? Our CFO is sensitive to variable token pricing and wants a clear worst-case.
- Discount ask: we are a small but fast-growing team; would you consider a 15% first-year credit if we commit to a 12-month spend target of $120k?

If it's helpful, procurement is on standby; DM me and I'll loop them in after we have a firm commercial recommendation.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform, MediSentry
procurement@medsentry.com

If you approve, I'll respond with those numbers and attach a revised quote.

Hi Alyssa — quick follow-up after our internal review. Answers below and a narrowed commercial offer: 

- Downgrade & KV cache: During the 2-week downgrade cooldown we will keep existing KV caches accessible in read-only mode. That lets your engineers query caches for debugging; note that new cache writes will route to the downgraded instance.

- RealTime Burst pricing (example):
  • Burst addon list price: $0.012 per token-equivalent for bursted tokens
  • For 50,000 tokens/day sustained over 30 days = 1.5M tokens/month -> list = $18,000/month
  • We propose a 10% usage discount at 50K/day -> $16,200/month as an upper bound for planning (you can set daily caps to control spend).

- Discount counter-proposal: We can offer a 12% first-year credit applied to monthly invoices if MediSentry signs a 12-month commitment with a $120k annual commit. This includes one 30-day pilot window with the same pricing and a single one-time migration credit of $5k to cover onboarding.

If that aligns, I'll issue an updated quote and DocuSign. If procurement wants a written SOW for the migration credit or a sample Cap table showing worst-case, I'm happy to include it.

Would you like me to set a calendar time to walk procurement through the burst calc and downgrade mechanics tomorrow?

Best,
